This narrative review serves as a review of previously published literature assessing the efficacy of traditional pharmacotherapy in treating AN while also exploring novel treatments, including dissociative anesthetics, psychedelics, cannabinoids, hormones, neurosteroids, and ketogenic nutrition.

Psilocybin, which stimulates serotonin 2A receptors and has received significant attention for its potential use in various psychiatric illnesses, could be useful to treat AN symptoms, but larger studies are still lacking.
In another study, Renelli et al. investigated the impact of ayahuasca compared to typical treatments for ED psychopathology in 13 individuals diagnosed with either AN (n = 8) or BN (n = 5) [81] .

The psychedelics taken varied, including psilocybin, lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD), ayahuasca, N-dimethyltryptamine (DMT), mescaline, and ibogaine. The results showed significant improvements in psychological wellbeing and depression when participants were assessed 2 weeks after taking psychedelics.
coverage_mentions.notes: Mentioned in the context of an online study of individuals with a lifetime ED diagnosis, showing improvements in depression.

coverage_mentions.supporting_quote: Ketamine appears to have rapid antidepressive and antisuicidal effects. Since most of the available studies concern unipolar depression, here we present a novel insight arguing that ketamine might be a promising treatment for bipolar disorder.

coverage_mentions.evidence_locator: S004 - Rapid Antisuicidal Effect of Ketamine
coverage_mentions.supporting_quote: A systematic review examining the effects of a single dose of ketamine on suicidal ideation concluded that it was able to rapidly reduce suicidal thoughts within 1 day.
The blockade of N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors (NMDARs) at inhibitory interneurons causes the disinhibition of pyramidal cells; this leads to the activation of glutamatergic transmission.

This suggests the use of ketamine as a viable treatment option for bipolar patients, given that ketamine increases BDNF expression although the exact mechanism of BDNF effect in bipolar disorder needs to be elucidated.

Evidence from preclinical studies has shown that ketamine rapidly induces synaptogenesis and reverses the synaptic changes caused by chronic stress, and that these actions are associated with its antidepressant effect.

One study found that ketamine produced an antidepressant effect by decreasing histone deacetylase activity in the nucleus accumbens of deprived rats; this suggested that ketamine may act via an epigenetic mechanism.
This effect may indicate an immunomodulatory role for ketamine in BD patients, who have a predisposition to autoimmune disease.
Thus, current evidence indicates that ketamine treatment improves gut microbiota composition, and mediates antidepressant effects through this mechanism.

coverage_mentions.supporting_quote: Recent clinical studies have shown that low-dose ketamine relieves depressive symptoms within hours, and it has been approved to treat treatment-resistant depression and suicidal ideation.

Low-dose ketamine treatment prior to chronic stress exposure reportedly protects animals from developing depressive behaviors (Brachman et al., 2016; McGowan et al., 2018) , suggesting that it augments stress resilience.

Rodent studies have also identified the roles of prefrontal D1 receptors as well as D1 receptor-expressing mPFC neurons projecting to multiple subcortical areas and dendritic spine formation in the mPFC for the sustained antidepressant-like effects of low-dose ketamine.

Although ketamine is an N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor antagonist developed as a dissociative anesthetic, low-dose ketamine administration paradoxically produces a rapid but transient increase in extracellular glutamate levels in the mPFC of rodents (Chowdhury et al., 2017; Moghaddam et al., 1997) via inhibiting NMDA receptors on inhibitory interneurons

as well as neuroplastic actions that improve functional connectivity in brain regions involved in chronic pain, are considered.

coverage_mentions.supporting_quote: New psychoactive substances (NPS) are a heterogeneous group of substances. They are associated with a number of health and social harms on an individual and societal level.
Synthetic hallucinogens (SH) include two main subcategories: hallucinogens and dissociatives.

Tryptamines are a group of monoamine alkaloids that are synthesised through decarboxylation of the amino acid tryptophan, and include compounds such as alpha-methyltryptamine (AMT), N,N-dimethyltryptamine (DMT), N,N-diallyl-5methoxytryptamine (5-MeO-DALT) and 5-methoxy-N,N-disopropyltyptamine (5-MeO-DIPT) 'foxy methoxy'.

Tryptamines are a group of monoamine alkaloids that are synthesised through decarboxylation of the amino acid tryptophan, and include compounds such as alpha-methyltryptamine (AMT), N,N-dimethyltryptamine (DMT), N,N-diallyl-5methoxytryptamine (5-MeO-DALT) and 5-methoxy-N,N-disopropyltyptamine (5-MeO-DIPT) 'foxy methoxy'.

Synthetic derivatives of the ergot alkaloid derivative lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD) such as 1-acetyl-LSD (ALD-52), 1-propionyl-LSD (1P-LSD) and 1-butyryl-LSD (1B-LSD) have been shown to have very different pharmacological profiles and may differ significantly in their effects.
The two main classes of dissociatives are arylcyclohexylamine [to which ketamine, phencyclidine (PCP) and methoxetamine (MXE) belong] and diarylethylamine.

Most hallucinogens share a common mechanism of 5-HT2A receptor modulation of serotoninergic activity, although there is an increasing understanding of the role of the glutamatergic system, and some dissociative hallucinogens also have activity at κ opioid receptors.
Phenethylamine derivatives interact mainly with cortical serotonin receptors, with the highest affinity for 5-HT2A receptors.
LSD analogues activate both 5-HT2A and 5-HT1A receptors.

Ketamine has a predominant action at the NMDA receptors whereas PCP, methoxetamine, 3-MeO-PCP, 4-MeO-PCP and 3-MeO-PCE have actions at serotonin receptors which may explain some of their additional toxicity.
